tagline: We make the best of beauty accessible to every eye, lip and face.
hero_kpi_rationale: The acquisition of rhode, a fast-growing lifestyle beauty brand, demonstrates an aggressive expansion strategy and integration of high-potential brands to accelerate future growth.

kpis.name: Acquisition of rhode
kpis.explanation: Announcement of an agreement to acquire the beauty brand rhode, including an initial payment and potential earn-out payments.
kpis.description: The agreement to acquire rhode for $800 million ($600M cash, $200M stock) plus potential earn-out of $200M underscores a significant external growth ambition.

kpis.name: Acquisition of Naturium
kpis.explanation: Completion of the acquisition of Naturium LLC for $333 million in cash and stock.
kpis.description: The acquisition of Naturium, a skincare brand, for $333 million in cash and stock demonstrates a strategy to broaden the portfolio of brands.
kpis.signal: Expansion through acquisition of complementary brands

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from the sale of beauty products, net of discounts and returns.
kpis.description: Net sales for fiscal year 2025 totaled $1,313.5 million, up 28.3% compared to fiscal year 2024 ($1,023.9M). This KPI is the primary indicator of business performance.

kpis.name: Gross Profit
kpis.explanation: Difference between net sales and cost of sales.
kpis.description: Gross profit for fiscal year 2025 totaled $935.7 million, up 29.2% compared to $724.1M in 2024. Gross margin remained stable at 71% of net sales.
kpis.signal: Profitability of sales before operating expenses

kpis.name: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs related to marketing, personnel, distribution and general overhead.
kpis.description: SG&A expenses for fiscal year 2025 totaled $777.7 million, up 35.4% compared to $574.4M in 2024. These expenses represent 59% of net sales.
kpis.signal: Investments to support growth and operations

kpis.name: Tariff Impact
kpis.explanation: Risk of additional costs due to tariffs on products imported from China (25% historical, new tariffs announced in 2025).
kpis.description: The company is exposed to significant tariff risks. The majority of products are manufactured in China and subject to 25% U.S. tariffs since May 2019. In March-April 2025, the Trump administration announced escalating additional tariffs. The company is considering global price increases and diversification of production sources.
kpis.signal: Risk related to international trade policies

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of 1.25 billion euros in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of 0.31 billion euros in the latest year

kpis.short: Net Sales - Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2025
kpis.name: Net Sales: Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2025
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from the sale of beauty products for fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: Net sales for fiscal year 2025 totaled $1,313.5 million, up 28.3% compared to fiscal year 2024.
kpis.signal: Business performance for the fiscal year

kpis.short: US Net Sales - Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2025
kpis.name: U.S. Net Sales: Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2025
kpis.explanation: Portion of net sales derived from the U.S. market for fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: The U.S. market represented 81% of total net sales for fiscal year 2025, confirming that the U.S. market is the company's primary growth driver.

kpis.short: International Net Sales - Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2025
kpis.name: International Net Sales: Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2025
kpis.explanation: Portion of net sales derived from international markets for fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: International markets represented 19% of total net sales for fiscal year 2025, primarily the United Kingdom and Canada, showing progressive growth internationally.

risks.title: Debt Levels
risks.score_rationale: The company has significant debt, with a total of $256.7 million in minimum principal payments due by March 31, 2030. This represents a significant risk to the company.

risks.title: Product Dependency
risks.score_rationale: The company is highly dependent on its products to generate revenue. A decline in demand or increased competition could impact sales.

risks.title: Credit Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company has significant credit commitments that could impact its ability to repay its debts.

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to regulations that could change and impact its business, particularly regarding cosmetics and labeling.

risks.title: Supply Chain Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company depends on its supply chain to produce and deliver its products. Disruptions in the supply chain could impact sales.

risks.title: Competition Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a competitive market where companies must constantly innovate and improve their products to remain competitive.

risks.title: Tariff Risks
risks.score_rationale: The majority of products are manufactured in China and subject to 25% U.S. tariffs since 2019. New tariffs announced in 2025 could increase costs significantly. The full impact remains to be assessed.

ai_positioning.summary: ELF does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
